articles.summary: Switch Metals Advances Lithium And Tantalum Exploration In Côte D’Ivoire  DirectorsTalk Interviews
articles.full_text:
Switch Metals plc (LON:SWT), the critical metals focused mining company with assets located in Côte d’Ivoire, has announced its unaudited interim results for the six months to 30 June 2026.
Highlights
• Continuation of our exploration programme largely at the Badinikro licence area in support of our maiden tantalum Mineral Resource Estimate;
• Activities included a discovery of lithium-rich spodumene zones at Issia where the Directors believe the Kabore discovery represents a material development for the Company;
• Tiassalé is also emerging as a standalone Lithium opportunity;
• Oversubscribed fundraise in May of £1.25 million (gross); available cash as at 30 June 2026 was £901,230; and
• We entered the second half of 2026 with an active RC drilling programme
Karl Akueson, CEO of Switch Metals, commented:
“We are particularly pleased with the successful funding and completion of our maiden drilling programme at Issia, an area with no previous systematic exploration for tantalum or lithium mineralisation located near a historic alluvial tantalum mine.
“The drilling of the Zraty and Kabore hard rock targets is central to our strategy at Issia where our objective is to delineate both a shallow resource to confirm early cash flow potential and to demonstrate significant upside from hard rock resources of both tantalum and lithium. We plan to generate and test additional shallow and hard rock targets to build a resource inventory in phases as the Issia project grows.
“Switch Metals controls 3,169 km² across three projects in Côte d’Ivoire and is not a single asset Company. By applying a systematic exploration process to these greenfield projects, we expect to be able to confirm and prioritise maiden drill targets in the near term, building toward a comprehensive picture of the scale and potential of our portfolio.”
Chairman’s Statement
Introduction
Switch Metals is building a district-scale critical minerals platform in Côte d’Ivoire, West Africa, focused on tantalum and lithium within one of the region’s most prospective LCT pegmatite corridors. The half year under review saw significant advancement of our exploration programme largely at the Badinikro licence area within the flagship Issia Project in support of our maiden tantalum Mineral Resource Estimate (“MRE”), now expected to be published early in the first quarter of 2027. This included the commissioning of a pilot wash plant to concentrate pit samples in support of our maiden tantalum MRE.
The Company has also made a discovery of lithium-rich spodumene zones at Kabore within Issia, with grades up to 2.8% lithium oxide (Li2O) confirming the presence of a working Lithium-Caesium-Tantalum (“LCT”) system at Issia.
The Directors believe the Kabore discovery represents a material development for the Company and complements the tantalum resources being advanced across the near surface eluvial, colluvial and drainage basin targets at Issia. The combination of tantalum and lithium within the same mineral system is a significant differentiator and substantially improves the long-term optionality of the project.
In addition, Tiassalé is also emerging as a standalone Lithium opportunity hosting over 990 km² of ground where the Company has already delineated multiple lithium soil anomalies. The next phase of work here is designed to generate maiden drill targets. The Company is a neighbour of Atlantic Lithium, under acquisition by Zhejiang Huayou Cobalt, and to Lithium Africa Corporation, affiliated with Ganfeng Lithium, providing an independent validation of the region’s prospectivity.
Operations and Use of Proceeds
While strengthened by the oversubscribed fundraise which completed in May of £1.25 million (gross at 10p a share) our focus remains on progressing the work programmes now underway. In particular, the RC drill results from the Zraty hard-rock tantalum target and Kabore lithium spodumene target at Issia.
Operationally, the net proceeds of the fund raise have been deployed as follows:
- Scout drilling campaign: to fund a maiden drill campaign at the Zraty and Kabore hard rock discoveries; and
- Mineral Resource Estimate advancement: to support the progression of tantalum MREs across the Company’s eluvial, colluvial and drainage basin targets at Issia.
Hard-Rock Drilling Programme
The Company commenced its maiden 2,500 metre RC drill programme at Issia in June 2026, testing two priority hard-rock pegmatite targets. Drilling at Zraty, one of the highest-grade hard-rock tantalum targets identified within the licence package, with surface samples returning up to 1,230 ppm Ta₂O₅, was completed first, with the rig subsequently moving to Kabore to test the 1.3 kilometre lithium spodumene anomaly below surface for the first time. RC drilling results for both targets are expected in the near term.
The Issia Project’s shallow placer tantalum mineralisation offers the potential for near-term ethical production from a stable, OECD-aligned West African jurisdiction, at a time of increasing scrutiny on DRC and Rwanda supply chains. In November 2025, the Company signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Xcelsior Capital Advisors and Wogen Resources, a global critical metals trader, covering a proposed strategic partnership for exploration funding, market access and ESG support, a direct signal of commercial interest in a traceable, ethically sourced tantalum supply from Côte d’Ivoire.
Outlook
The Company entered the second half of 2026 with the RC drilling programme now completed, a maiden resource programme at an advanced stage, and a growing body of geological evidence supporting the district-scale potential of its Côte d’Ivoire portfolio.
Financial review
The loss for the period, after finance costs and tax, of £696,256 (six months ended 30 June 2025: net loss of £1,003,432; year to 31 December 2025: net loss of £2,229,968), represents a loss of 0.57 pence per share (six month ended 30 June 2025: 1.24p; year to 31 December 2025: 2.24p).
Contained within these figures are administration costs of £667k and £16k project costs (excluding capitalised exploration expenditure). £128k of these expenses relate to Cote d’Ivoire and £26k of forex losses on translation.
In total, some £470k of funds were sent to Cote d’Ivoire in the first half of the year to support our projects which lifted the value of our Exploration & Evaluation (E&E) assets by a further £313k to £3.57m.
The results show financial performance for Switch Metals plc for the 6-month period combined with performance of Switch Metals CDI.
On the back of the £1.25m (gross) fund raise at 10p per share in May 2026, available cash as at 30 June 2026 was £901,230 (30 June 2025: £1,274,342; 31 December 2025: £536,199). The Company has no debt.

articles.full_text:
LNG Canada’s five shareholders have taken a final investment decision on Phase 2 of the Kitimat export terminal in British Columbia, clearing an expansion that will double production capacity to 28m tonnes a year.
The project will add two liquefaction trains, another LNG storage tank, a condensate tank, an additional loading berth and expanded utility and process systems at the terminal.
Shell, Petronas, PetroChina, Mitsubishi Corporation and Kogas are backing the expansion, which builds on infrastructure constructed for the first two-train phase.
Coastal GasLink will also expand the 670-km pipeline feeding Kitimat through five new compressor stations. Commercial operations from the expanded terminal are expected to begin in the early 2030s.

Hormuz disruptions push Murban crude to $109.40, Brent climbs sharply

WTI crude was at $93.05.
The rally, tracked by OilPrice, came as markets continued to assess disruption risks linked to the US-Iran conflict, the Strait of Hormuz and regional shipping security.
The sharpest move was in Murban, the UAE's flagship crude grade and an important reference for Asian refiners. Its jump above Brent indicates that traders are assigning a higher risk premium to Middle Eastern supply, particularly barrels exposed to Gulf shipping disruptions.

Crude flows through the Strait of Hormuz have recovered to about 13.2 million barrels per day, according to Kpler data cited by Trading Economics, while JPMorgan estimates that broader Middle East crude exports averaged 17.5 million bpd in September — about 98% of their pre-war level.

articles.title: New Pacific Link oil pipeline to B.C.'s coast officially declared a national priority - Daily Hive
articles.summary: New Pacific Link oil pipeline to B.C.'s coast officially declared a national priority  Daily Hive
articles.full_text:
The proposed new additional oil pipeline from near Edmonton to Metro Vancouver that would carry an additional one million barrels of crude a day to overseas markets is moving onto a faster federal government review track, with Prime Minister Mark Carney now aiming to finalize its conditions for construction by September 2027.
Carney announced today that the West Coast oil pipeline project, now formally called “Pacific Link,” has been designated a Project of National Interest under the federal Building Canada Act.
The pipeline would move Alberta oil to the West Coast for shipment to customers in Asia and other international markets, giving Canadian producers another outlet beyond the United States.

- Prime Minister Carney says $33-billion B.C. LNG expansion go-ahead shows Canada acting like an 'energy superpower'
- Federal plan aims to expand Port of Vancouver's terminals, railways, and trade capacity
The planned pipeline would take a southern route through British Columbia — avoiding the province’s North Coast and other sensitive coastal areas where a tanker ban remains in place.
Detailed route planning and environmental studies remain ahead. However, significant preliminary planning has already been conducted by Alberta’s provincial government, which has identified the southern route reaching Metro Vancouver as the preferred route. It would largely follow the same right-of-way/corridor already established by the Trans Mountain Pipeline, with the pipeline then traversing some of the southernmost areas of Metro Vancouver to reach a major new storage and marine export terminal in Tsawwassen, which would involve building a new additional causeway peninsula in the Strait of Georgia.
The federal government notes that it is also working with B.C.’s provincial government on building Vancouver Fraser Port Authority’s Roberts Bank 2 container terminal in Tsawwassen and on the future marine terminal to export oil from Pacific Link.
“Canada has a once-in-a-generation opportunity to become a global energy superpower,” said Carney.
“To create hundreds of thousands of good jobs. To transform our economy. To diversify our trade. To become less reliant on a single trade partner. To achieve greater strategic autonomy, so we can continue to live our lives as we choose. Pacific Link is critical to this mission.”
The prime minister is positioning the pipeline as part of its effort to double Canadian exports to countries other than the U.S.
The new designation establishes a single federal review process, with the Major Projects Office and Canada Energy Regulator tasked with developing the requirements the project must meet. Those conditions would cover matters such as environmental protection, Indigenous considerations, ownership, economic benefits, local hiring, and oversight. Carney’s September 2027 target is for completion of that work and clearing the way for major construction activities.
Meanwhile, the companies involved, the Alberta provincial government, and the federal government will also work on the project’s detailed design, cost estimates, route mapping, environmental surveys, equipment and material purchases, and workforce needs.
Trans Mountain Corporation would be responsible for developing, building, and operating Pacific Link on behalf of its backers. Pembina Pipeline Corporation is also involved, with the federal government identifying it as a private investor contributing expertise to the project’s development.
The federal government notes that it will have an equal ownership interest with Alberta’s provincial government, while First Nations will be offered an ownership stake of at least 10 per cent — supported by federal and Alberta provincial loan guarantee programs. Alberta’s provincial government is participating in the project through the Alberta Petroleum Marketing Corporation.
The federal government asserts that over 130 Indigenous communities near potential routes in Alberta and B.C. were consulted over the past three months while officials considered the national interest designation. The B.C. government was also consulted.
Alberta Premier Danielle Smith welcomed the decision, arguing that the pipeline would help Canadian energy reach more buyers and generate money for public services.
“This listing sends a clear message: Canada is ready to build again. We are ready to harness our strengths, seize new opportunities, and deliver the nation-building infrastructure our prosperity depends on,” said Smith.
Carney’s announcement today to prioritize and expedite Pacific Link also comes just weeks ahead of Alberta’s first separatism referendum. For many years, Alberta had been butting heads with previous federal administrations, particularly Justin Trudeau’s government, on pipeline proposals, with previous federal policies and strategies being a major contributing factor for growing some of the province’s independence sentiments.
“For too long, people across Canada have watched investment leave, projects stall, and opportunities slip away. Today, we are turning the page. Pacific Link represents a bold vision for Canada, one built on growth, confidence, and the understanding that Alberta energy should reach customers around the world,” continued Smith.
Her government estimates the project could support up to 140,000 jobs at the peak of construction, with the employment spread across Alberta and B.C. Operations, oil production, maintenance, and trade could support another 50,000 jobs annually.
The federal government estimates that Pacific Link would contribute more than $20 billion per year to Canada’s gross domestic product, and generate $100 billion in government revenue by 2060.
Smith’s administration has also released a longer-term royalty projection. They estimate that the additional oil production needed to supply the pipeline would generate more than $265 billion in extra provincial royalties over an expected operating life of more than 50 years.
In July 2026, under the new Canada-British Columbia Cooperative Prosperity Agreement, B.C. Premier David Eby announced his BC NDP-led provincial government had agreed to work with the Alberta and federal governments on the project’s routing and permitting. In exchange for the pipeline’s route through the province and the construction of a new marine export terminal, B.C.’s provincial government will gain a meaningful share of ongoing revenues from both the construction and operations of the new pipeline and terminal. As of the time of writing, the BC NDP have yet to issue a statement reacting to Carney’s recent decision.
Conservative Party of British Columbia leader Lorne Doerkson welcomed the federal government’s decision, asserting the provincial government should help other parts of Canada reach overseas buyers and benefit from the investment, jobs, and public revenue that major energy projects could bring.
“At a time of economic crisis, saying no to nation-building projects is not just bad policy, it’s, of course, un-Canadian,” said Doerkson during a press conference.
If elected premier, Doerkson said he would call for a working group with Alberta, the federal government, and First Nations to address environmental concerns and other issues surrounding the project.
“Protecting our coast and building our economy are not opposites. We can and we absolutely must do both,” he said.
Asked how he would respond to residents worried about construction near their homes or waterways, Doerkson acknowledged that parts of the route remain unclear and promised transparent discussions with residents and First Nations.
He also said some people he had spoken with saw the project as “a short-term inconvenience for long-term gain for the province.”
When asked whether the Conservatives, if they formed the next provincial government after the October 2026 provincial general election, would seek repeal of the northern oil tanker ban, Doerkson expressed concern about the restriction, but did not explicitly commit to removing it.
“I’m also very concerned about the notion that we simply just open everything up. I want to be very careful, very environmentally aware of what’s going on out there,” said the Conservative leader.
Beyond the oil pipeline, Doerkson promoted the Conservatives’ BC Energy Superpower Plan, which would aim to double B.C.’s natural gas production by 2032 and triple it by 2035.
He said a Conservative government would shorten permitting and approval timelines, seek international investment, and direct provincial ministries and agencies to work toward the production targets. He argued that greater energy revenues would help pay for hospitals, schools, and infrastructure while keeping taxes low.
The Greater Vancouver Board of Trade (GVBOT) also welcomed today’s announcement, saying broader access to overseas customers would make Canada less vulnerable to disruptions involving its existing trading partners.
Bridgitte Anderson, the president and CEO of GVBOT, said Pacific Link could help spur a wider wave of investment alongside LNG Canada’s second phase, mining and critical mineral projects, potash expansions, and transportation infrastructure, such as Roberts Bank Terminal 2.
Earlier this week, the private sector owners of LNG Canada made a business decision to proceed with the $33-billion second phase of their LNG production and export facility in Kitimat, B.C.

articles.title: Alaska LNG could cost more than double Gulf Coast rivals, raising questions over economics - WTVB
articles.summary: Alaska LNG could cost more than double Gulf Coast rivals, raising questions over economics  WTVB
articles.full_text:
By Curtis Williams
HOUSTON, Oct 1 (Reuters) – US President Donald Trump’s push to steer $54 billion of South Korean investment into Alaska LNG is putting a fresh focus on a 20 million-ton-a-year export project that would cost more than twice as much as a comparable US Gulf Coast plant.
Trump unveiled the plan on Wednesday as part of a broader $200 billion South Korean package. Seoul quickly said it had not yet decided whether to fund Alaska LNG and would first review the project’s commercial viability.
“The question is whether Asian buyers are willing to pay a premium in exchange for security of supply. So far, we have not seen evidence of that,” said Jason Feer, head of business intelligence at Poten & Partners.
Lead developer Glenfarne Group estimates Alaska LNG will cost $44.5 billion to $54.5 billion. That works out to roughly $2.2 billion to $2.7 billion per million metric tons per annum of capacity, by far the highest of any US export project ever proposed.
By comparison, the wave of US LNG projects approved since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine has generally been built at an average cost of about $1 billion per mtpa or less.
Cheniere Energy’s Corpus Christi Stage 3 expansion was estimated to cost about $8 billion for 10.5 mtpa of additional capacity, or roughly $760 million per mtpa.
Venture Global’s Plaquemines LNG project represented approximately $21 billion of investment for 20 mtpa, while NextDecade’s Rio Grande LNG and Woodside Energy’s Louisiana LNG are also near the $1 billion-per-mtpa threshold.
Gulf Coast export terminals tap extensive networks supplying shale gas from Texas, Louisiana and Appalachia. Alaska LNG would instead require an 800-mile (1,287-km) pipeline from the North Slope — a region in northern Alaska between the Brooks Range mountains and the Arctic Ocean — to Nikiski, estimated to cost $13.2 billion to $16.9 billion.
In addition to the pipeline, the project requires a large treatment plant on the North Slope before gas can be moved south for export. Glenfarne’s latest estimates place the cost of the treatment facility at $7.7 billion to $9.2 billion and the liquefaction terminal itself at $23.6 billion to $28.4 billion.
Alex Munton, director of global gas and LNG research at Rapidan Energy Group, said the project “may not be able to meet commercial thresholds for investment.”
Glenfarne did not immediately respond to a request for comment. On Wednesday, CEO Brendan Duval said Trump’s announcement would help bring “together the capital needed to accelerate Alaska LNG to a final investment decision and construction.”
Supporters say Alaska LNG’s location offers a strategic advantage because cargoes would reach key Asian importers such as Japan, South Korea and Taiwan significantly faster than Gulf Coast shipments, lowering shipping costs.
“Asia needs stable, secure supplies of gas and for that they may be willing to pay a premium,” said Jack Weixel at East Daley Analytics. He noted, however, that Canadian projects in the region could have advantages over Alaska LNG.
“These LNG developers should be looking at any and all options as the global market for natural gas, particularly among non-OECD nations, grows,” he said. “But, some will work better than others.”
(Reporting by Curtis Williams in Houston; Editing by Nathan Crooks and Bill Berkrot)

articles.full_text:
North of 60 Mining News - October 1, 2026
Pantheon Electric has increased recycled copper to 33% of its companywide feedstock, part of a multiyear effort to secure supplies of the conductive metal as electrification and AI infrastructure drive demand higher.
That initiative is anchored by Pantheon's mill in Leetsdale, Pennsylvania, which now recycles more than 100 million pounds of copper scrap into highly conductive products annually.
"Companies shouldn't have to choose between sustainability and performance," said Pantheon CEO Gregory Smith.
Pantheon, which is the largest independent producer of copper products for expanding electric grids in the United States, supplies wire and other electrification products to roughly 2,500 companies.
The company believes increasing the recycled content of its feedstock will help provide these customers with a more reliable source of copper as demand begins to challenge global supply.
In its "Copper in the Age of AI" report published earlier this year, S&P Global Energy & Market Intelligence forecasts annual copper demand will reach 42 million metric tons by 2040, a 50% rise from the roughly 28 million metric tons consumed globally in 2025.
Without a meaningful expansion of copper supply, S&P forecasts a potential 10-million-metric-ton annual shortfall by 2040.
Demand growth is being driven by the copper needed for electric vehicles, expanding power grids, renewable generation, AI-driven data centers, defense systems, and rising standards of living in developing economies.
While S&P expects recycled copper supply to more than double from roughly 4 million metric tons in 2025 to 10 million metric tons by 2040, that increase alone would not close the projected gap. The analytical firm estimates primary mined supply would need to climb from 23 million metric tons in 2025 to at least 32 million metric tons annually by 2040 to meet the balance of demand.
Recent developments in China underscore the pressures already emerging along the copper supply chain.
Analysts cited by Reuters in late September forecast China's refined copper output will rise only 3% to 3.4% in 2026, which would be its slowest growth in decades. Limited availability of copper concentrates and scrap are among the factors constraining the country's refiners.
Against this backdrop, Pantheon has been pushing toward a more circular supply chain that increases the reliability of its copper feedstock while lowering the carbon footprint of its products.
While copper is critical to wiring electrification projects meant to lower greenhouse gas emissions, turning raw copper ore into finished metal is energy intensive.
Recycled copper requires roughly 85% less energy than primary production and significantly reduces associated carbon emissions, according to the International Copper Association.
"Historically, recycled material has been treated as a fallback, something manufacturers turn to when mined supply gets tight rather than something they build a business around," said Smith. "That mindset is what leaves companies exposed as mining and the power grid struggle to keep pace with demand."
Pantheon says the reverberatory furnace at its Leetsdale facility strips impurities from scrap as it melts, allowing the mill to process lower-grade material that a conventional furnace could not handle without prior refining.
Every busbar, strip, sheet and plate produced at Leetsdale is manufactured from recycled copper, according to the company.
Slag from the furnace is sent off-site for additional copper recovery, further reducing the operation's waste stream.
Along with reducing energy use, Pantheon says increased recycling provides its customers with a domestic source of copper at a time when global processing capacity is heavily concentrated in China.
According to the U.S. Geological Survey, China produces roughly 44% of the world's refined copper.
Pantheon believes expanding its circular supply chain can help ensure customers continue receiving the copper products they need as global shortages intensify.
"The manufacturers who invest in circular supply are the ones who will still be delivering material five years from now," Smith said.

Southwest Research Institute has wrapped up work on a refined spark-ignited hydrogen internal combustion engine aimed at medium-duty commercial vehicles, Hydrogen Central reported. According to the source, the multiyear initiative yielded a powerplant that offers diesel-comparable torque and performance while releasing almost no carbon dioxide from its tailpipe.
Dr. Qilong Lu, a program manager within the institute's Powertrain Systems Engineering Department and a co-lead on the effort, noted that the organization brings decades of medium- and heavy-duty engine work and stands among the globe's foremost practitioners in creating and evaluating hydrogen ICEs for internal study, customers, and industry showcases. He also stated that the engine underwent design, build, and demanding testing at the institute to guarantee efficiency and performance.
Across a two-year span, the institute worked alongside a commercial customer and chosen Tier 1 suppliers to plan, engineer, and fabricate the engine. The opening phase encompassed development of both single-cylinder and multi-cylinder versions. The unit can be mounted in a commercial medium-duty truck chassis, supplying adequate torque and power to rival diesel-powered engines. Its foundation is a pent-roof-style architecture earlier created for gasoline combustion, subsequently tuned for hydrogen burning.
Lu described how the effort started with a single-cylinder approach centered on refining combustion and injection methods. The group then scaled up to build the complete multi-cylinder engine, tackling issues such as pre-ignition, combustion stability, and broader systems integration.
Altered port geometry within the engine enhances flow and aligns better with hydrogen's quicker combustion rates. A bigger intake valve boosts volumetric efficiency, while hydrogen-tailored fuel injectors add to improved combustion. A turbocharger is fitted to provide diesel-like torque output, and the package features an engine control system designed and calibrated by the institute.
Past institute-led efforts encompass a Class 8 heavy-duty hydrogen demonstration vehicle that turned a natural gas engine into a hydrogen ICE with only minor hardware changes. In a more recent step, engineers fitted the hydrogen ICE with a cutting-edge turbocharger to markedly boost performance, putting it on par with today's long-haul diesel engines while emphasizing fuel economy and preserving near-zero tailpipe emissions.
Chris Bitsis, assistant director of the institute's Powertrain Systems Engineering Department, who supervises combustion research programs, remarked that the undertaking united numerous disciplines and specialists across the institute. He added that the hydrogen combustion engine program strives daily to push the technology forward and highlight its promise as an industry answer with near-zero carbon emissions.

Long-Term Copper Targets Take Center Stage
Southern Copper drew attention as October opened after signaling that it had surpassed its output goal for the year while laying out an ambitious plan to lift copper production across the coming decade. The update placed the producer at the center of the copper conversation just as the metals and mining group held the market spotlight.
The plan matters because it frames how one of the lowest-cost copper producers aims to grow supply over a long horizon through a slate of major projects. Lifting output on this scale would deepen the company's standing across the Americas, where it operates large mines in Peru and Mexico.
Framing the plan around the coming decade also sends a signal about direction. Rather than lean only on existing mines, the company has pointed toward measured expansion through flagship projects, a choice that speaks to how it reads demand for copper across the energy transition.
What Metals And Mining Standing Means Here
A metals and mining label applies to companies that extract and process raw materials, and Southern Copper sits among the most recognizable copper names in that group. Its reach spans mining, smelting and refining across Peru and Mexico.
Within the broader Metals and Mining Stocks space, the company stays closely watched across the US equity market. Southern Copper shares trade on the New York Stock Exchange, placing the stock within the NYSE Composite.
Firms carrying this designation tend to move with the prices of the commodities they produce, which can swing with global demand, ore grades and supply conditions. That sensitivity gives copper names a distinct rhythm compared with steadier corners of the market.

Inside Southern Copper's Core Operations
Southern Copper runs large mining operations across Peru and Mexico, anchored by sites such as Cuajone and Toquepala in Peru and a cluster of mines in Mexico. The company extracts copper alongside byproducts including molybdenum, zinc and silver.
Beyond extraction, the firm operates smelting and refining capacity that turns ore into marketable metal. This vertical reach means the company touches several stages of the copper chain, which helps it capture value from pit to finished metal.
The plan to lift output through flagship projects underscores how the company treats long-horizon growth as a lasting pillar. That emphasis clarifies how management views the breadth of the franchise at a moment when copper sits at the center of electrification.
Each of these arms feeds the others. Scale in mining supports steady feed for smelters, while processing capacity moves the firm closer to finished metal, creating a web of connections that reinforces the whole enterprise.

Central to the growth plan is the Tia Maria project in Peru, slated to begin production in the coming years and add meaningfully to copper output. Alongside it sit a slate of developments in Mexico that the company has lined up to lift total production over the decade.
These projects speak to a long-horizon approach. Bringing a major site online takes years of permitting, construction and ramp-up, and the company has framed its plan around a sequence of such developments rather than a single step.
If the slate advances as described, the company could lift copper output substantially across the decade. That prospect has become a defining theme in how the firm presents the scope for growth from a base of large, long-life assets.

Demand threads run through many channels at once. Expanding power grids, data-center build-outs and electrified transport all lean on copper, while supply has been slow to catch up given the long lead times needed to bring new mines online.

This cost standing also shapes how the company funds its growth plan. A business that produces copper efficiently has more room to commit capital to long-horizon projects, linking the cost story directly to the decade-long expansion.
Keeping costs contained is an ongoing effort rather than a fixed state, since grades, energy prices and labor all shift over time. The company leans on scale, favorable ore bodies and steady operations to defend its standing, treating cost control as a discipline that underpins both today's output and the projects it has mapped for the years ahead.
Production Shifts And Ore Grades
Recent quarters have seen copper output ease at some Peruvian operations, driven by lower ore grades at sites such as Cuajone. Grade shifts are a normal feature of mining, since the richness of ore changes as a deposit is worked through over time.
Even so, the company has pointed to having surpassed its output goal for the year, a sign that strength elsewhere helped offset softness at certain mines. Managing grade across a portfolio of sites is a constant task for a large producer.

Against that macro frame, copper carried a firm tone even as parts of the precious-metals complex softened and gold miners traded on firmer bond yields. That split within the metals complex placed copper-heavy names in a different light from their gold-focused peers.
Macro conditions do not move a producer of this size on their own, yet they set the stage on which company-specific news plays out. A calmer rate picture paired with firm copper tends to make the market more receptive to the long-dated promise embedded in mining expansion.
Competitive Landscape For Southern Copper
Southern Copper competes with other large copper producers spread across the Americas, Africa and the Asia-Pacific region. Each races to control high-grade ore, secure permits and bring new capacity online at a pace that can keep up with demand.
This rivalry shapes how the company directs its effort and times its expansions. The decade-long plan can be read in part as a move to strengthen its standing at a moment when supply security has climbed the agenda for many buyers of the metal.
Competition also keeps the pace of change brisk. Each advance from a rival in grade, scale or cost control tends to draw a response, and that back-and-forth has sharpened as copper moves to the center of how miners distinguish themselves.

Why Did Panoro Minerals Ltd. (TSXV:PML) Fall by -3.59% on 30 September, 2026?
Panoro Minerals shares declined -3.59% on September 30, confirming renewed downside pressure after an uneven month for TSXV:PML. Market data show that the stock had already experienced several weaker sessions during September, indicating that volatility and profit-taking were influencing short-term momentum.
There does not appear to be a clearly identified negative company announcement explaining the September 30 decline. Recent corporate developments have instead remained centered on advancing Cotabambas.
Panoro recently announced that South Pit drilling continued to intersect high-grade mineralization at Cotabambas. The company also signed a cooperation agreement with the Municipality of Cotabambas during September, adding another element to its community-engagement and project-advancement strategy.
Consequently, the latest share-price weakness appears more consistent with valuation reassessment, profit-taking and volatile sentiment toward development-stage Mining companies rather than a clearly documented deterioration in the underlying project.
The Business model of Panoro Minerals Ltd.
Panoro operates an exploration and mineral-development business model.
The company's strategy involves identifying and advancing copper-rich mineral systems in Peru, with Cotabambas representing its principal development opportunity. Exploration drilling is intended to expand mineralization, improve geological confidence and support increasingly detailed engineering and economic work.
Panoro's strategy also includes monetizing non-core assets and redirecting Capital toward Cotabambas. Proceeds received from a previous non-core asset transaction have provided additional funding for drilling, exploration, permitting and engineering activities.
Unlike an established mining producer, Panoro's core value proposition is therefore based primarily on increasing the scale and quality of its mineral resources and moving Cotabambas toward potential development.
Key Reasons Behind Decline
Profit-Taking: Panoro has generated significant investor interest as drilling and project advancement have progressed. Following stronger periods, shareholders may lock in gains, creating temporary selling pressure.
Valuation Sensitivity: Positive exploration results can rapidly increase expectations for development-stage miners. When substantial future project success becomes reflected in market valuations, shares can become more vulnerable to corrections.
Development Risk: Cotabambas still requires substantial technical, engineering, permitting and financing work before commercial production could become a reality.
Copper-Price Exposure: Panoro's investment thesis is strongly connected to copper. Structural Demand from electrification and grid investment remains supportive, but Recession concerns or weaker industrial activity could negatively affect near-term copper sentiment.
Funding Requirements: Large-scale copper development can require considerable capital. Panoro has strengthened its funding position through financing and asset-sale proceeds, but future development could still require significant additional resources.
Peruvian Exposure: Concentration in Peru introduces political, regulatory, permitting and community-relations risks that investors need to incorporate into their assessment.
Geopolitical Uncertainty: US-Iran tensions and broader geopolitical instability can increase energy prices and inflationary pressures. Higher fuel, construction and equipment costs could negatively influence future mine-development economics, while weaker global growth could pressure copper demand expectations.
Risks Investor Needs to Consider
Project execution remains fundamental. Encouraging drilling must eventually translate into technically and economically viable development plans.
Permitting represents another material consideration because large mining projects require extensive regulatory and environmental approvals.
Community relations are especially important in Peru. Panoro's recent agreements demonstrate continued engagement, but maintaining long-term stakeholder support remains essential.
Investors should additionally consider financing risk, commodity-price volatility, political uncertainty, infrastructure requirements and potential construction-cost inflation.
What Is the Dividend Outlook?
Panoro Minerals is oriented toward project development rather than income generation.
Available capital is expected to remain focused on drilling, resource expansion, engineering, permitting and advancement of Cotabambas.
The Shareholder proposition therefore centers on potential project value creation rather than regular dividend distributions.
What Does the ESG Investment Case Look Like?
Copper has a potentially supportive long-term ESG demand profile because it is essential for electricity networks, renewable-energy infrastructure and electrification.
However, developing a large copper project creates significant environmental responsibilities. Water management, biodiversity, land disturbance, waste management and eventual reclamation will require careful oversight.
Social engagement is equally important. Panoro's recent cooperation agreement with the Municipality of Cotabambas provides evidence of continuing efforts to maintain relationships with local stakeholders.
Governance considerations include disciplined capital allocation, transparent technical disclosure and responsible management of project-development risks.
What Are the Bull and Bear Cases for TSXV:PML?
Bull Case:
Cotabambas provides Panoro with substantial exposure to copper, gold and silver within an established mining region of southern Peru.
Recent drilling continues to support resource-growth opportunities, while ongoing metallurgy, engineering and future economic work could progressively reduce uncertainty around development. The company is currently advancing Cotabambas across multiple workstreams.
Long-term copper demand associated with electrification, grid investment and data-center infrastructure could provide a supportive Commodity backdrop.
Bear Case:
Cotabambas remains a development-stage project with significant work required before commercial mining.
Large copper projects can require substantial capital, making financing conditions important for future shareholder outcomes.
Political developments, permitting delays, community challenges or disappointing technical results could slow advancement.
Weak copper markets or global recessionary conditions could also pressure valuation even if Panoro continues making operational progress.
Technical Levels to Watch
- Support Zone: Investors should monitor whether PML can establish a stable trading base after the latest selling pressure.
- Resistance Levels: Previous areas associated with stronger selling could limit early recovery attempts.
- Volume Trends: Increasing Volume accompanying declines could suggest stronger distribution, while improving participation during rebounds would provide a healthier signal.
- Momentum Indicators: September trading has been volatile, leaving short-term momentum fragile and increasing the importance of sustained stabilization.
Outlook
Panoro Minerals continues to advance Cotabambas through exploration, engineering and community engagement. Recent drilling provides further geological support for the project's resource-growth strategy, while previous financing and non-core asset monetization have strengthened the company's ability to pursue an expanded work program.
Nevertheless, the September 30 decline illustrates the volatility inherent in development-stage copper equities. Positive drilling alone cannot eliminate financing, permitting, execution and commodity-price risks.
Long-term copper fundamentals could provide a constructive backdrop if electrification, grid expansion and data-center investment continue supporting demand. Near-term macroeconomic uncertainty and geopolitical tensions, however, could keep commodity equities volatile.
The outlook for TSXV:PML therefore remains cautious and balanced. Cotabambas offers meaningful long-term development potential, but investors will continue assessing drilling progress, engineering work, funding requirements and the company's ability to steadily reduce project risk.

articles.title: LNG Canada Owners Commit $33 Billion to Double Kitimat Export Capacity - Business Examiner
articles.summary: LNG Canada Owners Commit $33 Billion to Double Kitimat Export Capacity  Business Examiner
articles.full_text:
LNG Canada's ownership group has approved a second phase at its Kitimat terminal, with up to 4,000 construction jobs expected at peak, Daily Hive reported. The federal government says the project will release $33 billion in private investment.
Prime Minister Mark Carney welcomed the final investment decision on Tuesday. Phase 2 will lift annual capacity from 14 million to 28 million tonnes. Phase 1 began exporting in June 2025.
What the Expansion Adds
The project includes two processing units, another LNG storage tank, an additional loading berth and supporting equipment. The Kitimat expansion will also add about 90 full-time and 150 contractor positions to the permanent workforce once complete.
Ottawa describes it as the second-largest single private investment in Canadian history. It says the expansion would make LNG Canada the second-largest facility of its kind in the world.
Carney's government referred the project to the federal Major Projects Office in September 2025. Support for it also appeared in the July 2026 cooperation agreement between Carney and Premier David Eby.
Pipeline Upgrade and Ownership
The decision clears the way for a multibillion-dollar capacity increase on Coastal GasLink. That is the 670-km pipeline running from the Dawson Creek area to Kitimat. TC Energy says new compressor stations and upgrades will nearly double the volume it can carry.
Construction is expected to start in early 2027. The upgraded line should be in service in the early 2030s. TC Energy estimates up to 2,100 workers at peak across five sites.
Shell Canada holds 40 per cent of LNG Canada. Petronas owns 25 per cent. PetroChina and Mitsubishi Corporation own 15 per cent each, and Kogas holds five per cent.
First Nations Option and Local Contracts
The Gitga'at, Gitxaała, Haisla, Kitselas and Kitsumkalum First Nations can invest up to $1 billion through MNT Investments LP. In return they would get a majority stake in the new 225,000-cubic-metre storage tank.
The tank would be leased back to the project, giving the nations a long-term revenue stream.
Ottawa says LNG Canada has already awarded more than $4.9 billion in contracts to Indigenous-owned and local firms. Coastal GasLink's contracts with such businesses total more than $1.8 billion.
Political and Business Reaction
Carney said the project was built in partnership with Indigenous Peoples. He said it will send some of the lowest-emitting LNG to Asian markets. Global News reported he also described the expansion as a secure supply source for Asia and Europe.
Eby called the decision a big win for jobs and long-term prosperity that will help fund public services. The BC NDP said some provincial revenue from the project will go to climate programs.
It also cited projections that the facility's emissions will be 35 per cent below the best-performing LNG plants and 60 per cent below the global average.
Claire Rattée, the Conservative candidate for Skeena, welcomed the decision. But she said B.C. needs many more like it. She blamed red tape and uncertain permitting under the NDP for stalled or abandoned projects.
The Conservative platform calls for more than doubling B.C. gas production by 2032 and more than tripling it by 2035. It also proposes a 120-day permitting law for major projects.
Bridgitte Anderson, president and CEO of the Greater Vancouver Board of Trade, said the project shows what governments, Indigenous partners and industry can achieve together.
Citing LNG Canada's estimates, the board said Phase 2 could generate more than $50 billion in government revenue over its life.
The board has identified more than $230 billion in potential major investments across B.C. It wants faster permitting and greater Indigenous ownership participation.

articles.title: Lithium: Is it Nigeria’s new oil or an old mistake? - Punch Newspapers
articles.summary: Lithium: Is it Nigeria’s new oil or an old mistake?  Punch Newspapers
articles.full_text:
Oil was supposed to change everything. It didn’t. It made us a major exporter who imported refined petrol, a billion-dollar earner whose oil communities drank polluted water. The United Nations Environment Programme said it would take 25 to 30 years and $1bn just to start cleaning Ogoniland.
Now, lithium has put Nigeria back on the global map.
Last July, President Bola Tinubu inaugurated what the government described as West Africa’s largest lithium processing plant in Nasarawa. Less than three months later, the United Nations announced it had selected Nigeria, alongside Guinea, Indonesia, Madagascar, Zambia and Zimbabwe, as one of the first countries to receive country-level support under its new initiative on critical energy transition minerals.
The world is scrambling. Demand for lithium, copper, nickel, cobalt and rare earth elements is expected to almost triple by 2030.
For Nigeria, lithium is at the centre of this new attention. On paper, the proposition is attractive. The UN says its mechanism will help mineral-rich countries strengthen value addition, diversify economies, improve transparency, protect communities and ensure the benefits of the energy transition are shared fairly. Secretary-General António Guterres has repeatedly made the point that countries and communities endowed with these resources must first benefit from them.
But Nigerians have heard promises about the transformative power of natural resources before. Oil was going to change everything. Decades after becoming a major oil producer, the country still struggled to build the industrial capacity to fully process the resource it was exporting.
Now that Nigeria’s lithium has arrived at the centre of global attention, it may be smaller than oil in today’s economy, but the question is identical: Will Nigeria use the world’s demand for lithium to build something at home, or will it once again be satisfied with extracting and exporting what others need?
This is even as the UN announcement does not explain how the partnership will work in practice or what it will mean for Nigeria. What will the United Nations and other international actors help Nigeria to do? Will the support help Nigeria process lithium locally, develop battery-related industries, acquire technology and train Nigerians for the emerging industry? Will it strengthen mining regulation, attract investment into manufacturing, create skilled and decent employment, and help Nigerian businesses enter the mineral value chain?
Lithium did not suddenly become valuable. For decades, coal, oil and gas-powered industries, transport and electricity, but climate concerns, energy security and vulnerable fossil-fuel supply chains are pushing countries towards renewable electricity, electric vehicles, battery storage and, increasingly, nuclear power. More than 40 countries now include nuclear energy in their strategies, with over 70GW under construction globally, while the IEA expects nuclear capacity to grow by at least one-third by 2035. This transition is not ending dependence on natural resources; it is shifting it to minerals.
That is why the rush for batteries matters. Lithium is central to rechargeable batteries, with electric vehicles and battery storage accounting for about 90 per cent of today’s lithium-ion battery market. Lithium-ion battery deployment increased more than sixfold between 2020 and 2025. Electric-vehicle battery deployment reached 1.2TWh in 2025, nearly 30 per cent higher than the previous year, while 108GW of new battery storage was deployed, up 40 per cent from 2024. The IEA says lithium demand has risen by about 25 per cent annually over the past two years, while the UN Trade and Development projects a 353 per cent increase between 2024 and 2040.
Yet lithium is only part of the wider mineral economy. Copper powers electrification; nickel, cobalt and graphite support batteries; rare earths are used in electric motors and wind turbines, while growing data-centre and semiconductor demand is adding pressure. The economic stakes are higher because processing creates far more value than extraction: UNCTAD found refined lithium, graphite, nickel and cobalt were worth several times their raw forms in 2022. Yet Australia and Chile produced more than half of global lithium in 2024, while China dominates processing of several critical minerals. That is where the real money is made.
So, why are investors coming to Nigeria? It begins with geology. Lithium-bearing pegmatites have been identified in Nasarawa, Kaduna, Kogi, Kwara, Oyo, Ekiti, Cross River and parts of the Federal Capital Territory, with Nasarawa emerging as the centre of the current rush. Endo, Udege, Kokona and Keffi are among the areas attracting activity.
Geological studies indicate varying grades, from below 0.5 per cent to as high as 13 per cent lithium oxide, although many reported deposits fall around 2.5 to 5 per cent. Claims of 20 million tonnes of ore at about 6 per cent Li2O in parts of Nasarawa and up to 50 million tonnes across the wider area have also circulated, but Nigeria does not yet have one nationally established lithium reserve figure. Most deposits still require systematic drilling to establish their commercially recoverable resources.
Artisanal and small-scale operations and larger companies are already mining. Ganfeng Lithium has developed an open-pit operation at Endo, while Jupiter Lithium and US-based ReElement Technologies are exploring a 442-square-kilometre area and targeting a 55,000-tonne annual spodumene concentrate operation. Thor Explorations, through Newstar Lithium, has also secured more than 600 square kilometres across Oyo, Kwara and Ekiti. Investment has moved into processing: China’s Avatar New Energy Materials commissioned a plant in Nasarawa with a reported 4,000-tonne daily capacity in 2024; Canmax announced a $200m project, and Diamond New Energy, with Jiuling Lithium and Canmax, commissioned a 6,000-tonne-per-day facility at Endo in 2026, backed by about $250m. The government has also announced or supported proposed projects involving hundreds of millions of dollars, including lithium processing and battery manufacturing.
The investors now span Chinese, British-linked, American, Canadian and Nigerian interests, including Avatar, Ganfeng, Jiuling, Canmax, Jupiter Lithium, ReElement, Thor Explorations and Lithium King. Yet the country’s actual earnings remain difficult to establish. Government figures show solid-minerals revenue rising from N6 billion in 2023 to more than N38bn in 2024, but this covers the entire sector, not lithium. NEITI’s 2023 audit recorded China as Nigeria’s largest mineral export destination, receiving 176,352 tonnes of minerals, including lithium and spodumene, but it did not report a separate lithium export value. Nigeria therefore has deposits, miners, processors and foreign investors, but still lacks a transparent national picture showing exactly how much lithium is being extracted, exported and converted into public revenue.
Even if investors bring processing plants, capital and jobs, Nigeria may still capture only a fraction of its lithium’s value. The UN warns that weak governance and irresponsible extraction could leave resource-rich communities bearing environmental and human costs without significant economic benefits. Its new critical-minerals initiative therefore aims to support value addition, diversification and fairer benefit sharing. The question is how much value will actually be created and retained in Nigeria.
The lithium chain runs from mining and processing to refining, battery materials, batteries, electric vehicles and energy storage. Nigeria has begun moving beyond extraction, including through the 6,000-tonne-per-day Nasarawa plant inaugurated in July 2026, but processing is only one stage. Who owns the facilities? Where does the material go? How much technology, capital, skilled employment and supply-chain participation remain Nigerian? Job numbers alone are insufficient: wages, safety, workers’ rights, child and forced labour, and environmental exposure matter. So do the costs to mining communities through land loss, pollution, water contamination and displacement. Who bears those costs, and who captures the value when Nigerian lithium becomes somebody else’s industrial input?
That brings us to the role of government and whether the rules are strict enough. Nigeria already has rules covering mining licences, royalties, environmental obligations and Community Development Agreements. The Mining Act requires mining companies to enter agreements with host communities covering issues such as employment, training, infrastructure and environmental management.
The harder question, however, is enforcement. Nigeria’s experience with oil makes the concern unavoidable. The country has had decades to develop systems to turn natural resources into jobs, public revenue and broader economic development, yet resource wealth has not automatically produced those outcomes. Oil generated enormous revenues: NEITI records oil and gas revenue of $52.8bn in 2024, compared with $45.2bn in 2023.
Yet for decades, Nigeria remained primarily an exporter of crude while importing much of the refined petroleum it consumed. Between 2020 and 2024, petroleum-product imports averaged about 376,000 barrels per day, even as crude remained one of the country’s principal exports. Domestic refining capacity was allowed to deteriorate for years; crude supplied to Nigerian refineries was negligible in 2021 and 2022 before rising sharply with the commissioning of the Dangote refinery.
The environmental cost was equally severe. UNEP’s assessment of Ogoniland found widespread contamination after more than 50 years of oil operations, including polluted soil, groundwater, drinking water, creeks and mangroves. PETRONAS takes steps to maintain gas supply
The disruption of the Songkhla gas pipeline could have effects on gas supplies to customers in Malaysia and Thailand given this scenario, PETRONAS it implemented measures to maintain continuity of supply, especially in the Malaysian market.

Support for the proposed hydrogen network outweighed opposition by around five to one after residents were given details of the project, while 61% backed government investment in cleaner local energy.
Research commissioned by Humber Hydrogen reveals that people in Yorkshire and the Humber feel left behind, citing the decline of traditional industries for the lack of new jobs and economic growth. Residents see clean energy industries, particularly projects such as Humber Hydrogen, as a significant opportunity to create jobs, attract investment and support economic renewal across the region.
The report by Humber Hydrogen and More in Common – The case for hydrogen in the Humber: Results from polling and focus groups – was launched at the Yorkshire and Humber Regional Reception at the Labour Party Conference on Saturday 26 September. Government ministers heard how locating Britain’s first hydrogen cluster in the Humber could support thousands of jobs and attract significant investment to Britain.
Leading energy companies behind Humber Hydrogen are calling on the UK Government to open the competition for Britain's first hydrogen network at the Autumn Budget, warning that further delays risk undermining industry confidence and delaying investment, jobs and growth in the Humber. Senior leaders have said that without opening this competition the Humber could miss out on this vital opportunity to retain industry and attract investment to the region.
Economic analysis commissioned by Humber Hydrogen shows that Britain's first hydrogen cluster in the Humber could support more than 54,000 jobs during construction, safeguard up to 4,000 jobs in key industries such as steel and chemicals, support 700 apprenticeships and generate £17 billion of economic growth.
Key data provided by the More in Common report shows that:
- Residents are concerned about future opportunities for young people. 75 per cent say there are few employment opportunities for young people and 88 per cent of 18-24 year-olds say opportunities for young people are lacking. More than half (51 per cent) of people from the region think their local area is worse than it was ten years ago, with many blaming the deterioration of the local area on the decline of traditional industries.
- Whilst people in Yorkshire and the Humber express scepticism about net zero, they are supportive of investment in clean energy as a credible route to bring back jobs, deliver economic growth and regional prosperity. While just 41 per cent support the UK's net zero target, most residents in Yorkshire and the Humber think that government investment in generating cleaner forms of energy in their local area would be a good thing (61 per cent).
- After the Humber Hydrogen project was explained to residents, support for Humber Hydrogen outweighed opposition by around five to one.
- The call for investment extends beyond the East Coast of England. The British public also support investment in the region, with 34 per cent of Britons saying increased investment in less prosperous areas of Britain like Yorkshire and the Humber would benefit the whole country.
Speaking in a focus group, Nelson from Doncaster said:
“I think one of the problems with a lot of northern places, northern cities, is the fact that people have to go to other cities like Leeds and Manchester in order to get high paying jobs. And to stop that, we need better jobs in the region.”
Speaking on behalf of the cluster, Ian Radley, Chief Commercial Officer at National Gas, said:
“People across Yorkshire and the Humber are calling on renewed investment in the region's industries to secure skilled opportunities for the next generation. Humber Hydrogen can help deliver this ambition by creating and attracting new jobs, supporting industry and driving economic growth.
“We’re calling on the UK Government to back the Humber as the home of Britain’s first hydrogen cluster. The region already has the industrial base, skills and infrastructure to lead Britain's hydrogen economy.
“The Autumn Budget is a pivotal moment to provide industry with greater certainty about the future of hydrogen in Britain. Without clear policy support, Britain risks missing a significant investment opportunity, putting jobs, key industries and our position as a global leader in hydrogen at risk."
Hydrogen can enhance Britain’s energy security by providing flexible, cleaner energy for our power system and industries. As an alternative fuel to natural gas, it can be used to decarbonise power generation and hard-to-electrify industries such as heavy manufacturing, chemicals and steel production. It can also be used as a feedstock for high-value products such as ammonia and Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF).
The first-of-its-kind hydrogen cluster in East Yorkshire and North Lincolnshire would be delivered by four of Britain’s leading energy companies – Centrica, Equinor, National Gas, and SSE Thermal. Together they bring expertise in hydrogen transport, production, usage and storage to support the region’s industries, reduce emissions, and create jobs.
The Humber is the leading candidate for the UK Government’s £500 million Hydrogen Transport and Storage Business Model thanks to its strong hydrogen industry and potential with:
- Six power stations in the region, investing in more than 4GW hydrogen-to-power – that’s more than 10 per cent of Britain’s average electricity demand.
- Two blue and five green hydrogen projects, owned by different producers, delivering approximately 3GW of low carbon hydrogen.
- 65 per cent of the UK’s total potential new-build storage capacity for hydrogen is in East Yorkshire. Natural salt caverns at Aldbrough are already used for gas storage and will be adapted and expanded with new caverns for hydrogen storage, helping to create one of the largest facilities of its kind in the world.
You can download the full report here.
Further quotes from those who participated in the focus group conversations.
"I think it would be a good investment… Obviously if it becomes the hydrogen hub and apparently hydrogen is meant to be the future… then you're obviously going to attract more people to the area. And with more people in the area, obviously that causes your high streets and everything to thrive." Cian, Accountant (Food Manufacturer)
“If it brings employment, then it can only be a good thing. If you’ve got people with degrees that are able to help assist with that, then they will stay in that area or come back if they’ve done and got a degree, they’ll come back to the Humber region and they’ve got money then to spend. So it all helps with the economy.” Martha, Admin, Scunthorpe
More in Common research methodology
These findings are based on a mixed methods research project involving nationally representative quantitative research across Great Britain, and separate, regionally representative quantitative research across the Yorkshire and the Humber. More in Common was commissioned to conduct this research by National Gas on behalf of Humber Hydrogen. More in Common is a member of the British Polling Council and abides by their rules. Data Tables can be found on More in Common’s website.
The regional Yorkshire and Humber poll had a sample size of 1,552, including 240 Yorkshire and the Humber residents who had a connection to the energy sector. Fieldwork for this poll took place between 04-18 August 2026. The national poll had a sample size of 2,010. Fieldwork for this poll took place between 14-17 August 2026. The regional poll was weighted to be representative of Yorkshire and the Humber according to age and gender interlocked, ethnicity, education level and 2024 General Election vote. The national poll was weighted according to age and gender interlocked, region, 2024 General Election vote, ethnicity, and education level.
Three focus groups were conducted in Yorkshire and the Humber area across two rounds of research.
The first was with residents with a connection to the energy sector.
The second and third were with 2024 Labour voters who were considering Reform and 2024 Conservative voters who were considering Reform.
These groups took place on 30 July and 27 August 2026.
The names of focus group participants have been changed.

articles.summary: China halts fuel exports, pushing Brent crude above $100  Yahoo Finance
articles.full_text:
Brent crude climbed above $100 a barrel on Thursday after Chinese refiners suspended fuel exports for October, according to Reuters, piling pressure on energy markets already disrupted by the U.S.-Iran war and Ukraine's attacks on Russian refining infrastructure. Brent crude with December expiry was last trading 2.2% higher at $100.15 per barrel, having earlier fallen 1%, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate with November expiry rose 1.5% to $91.74.
Beijing began a week-long national holiday on Thursday without issuing export permits to major refiners, allowing shipments only to Hong Kong and Macau, according to Reuters, citing four unnamed sources. The sources said they could not confirm whether export permits would be granted again once the holiday concludes on October 7, noting that domestic fuel inventories and refining output would probably factor into any decision.
PetroChina, the state-owned oil giant, scrapped several October cargo commitments for gasoline and jet fuel, Reuters reported. Privately held Zhejiang Petrochemical Corp also scheduled no oil product shipments during the holiday week.
Beijing restricted fuel exports in March after the Iran war disrupted Middle Eastern crude supplies, then relaxed those curbs in July and began managing diesel, gasoline, and jet fuel shipments on a monthly basis. Commercial gasoil and diesel inventories sit roughly 20 million barrels below the threshold Beijing has set for permitting exports, with gasoline about 9 million barrels short, according to Reuters, citing Zameer Yusof, a senior manager for clean oil products at data firm Kpler.
Michal Meidan, who leads China energy research at the Oxford Institute for Energy Studies, said that the suspension reflected Beijing's prioritization of domestic fuel supply. "International markets are an afterthought," Meidan said.
The suspension follows Chinese President Xi Jinping's trip to Washington, during which President Donald Trump pressed Xi to help bring global fuel supplies under control. The Trump administration has told Germany and France to draw down emergency diesel inventories or face a potential U.S. diesel export ban. According to the outlet, Energy Secretary Chris Wright said diesel exports from the Middle East and China had been lost to global markets, and that Washington was anticipating announcements from Europe regarding new diesel supplies.
The suspension adds to an already strained supply picture. The Trump administration issued a solicitation Tuesday for the final 40-million-barrel tranche of a 172-million-barrel Strategic Petroleum Reserve release authorized in March, part of a broader International Energy Agency drawdown. U.S. diesel prices have reached a record roughly $6.50 a gallon — about 70% above pre-war levels — while gasoline averages around $4.45 a gallon nationally.
Concerns about crude availability have softened since Saudi Arabia brought its East-West Pipeline back online and tanker departures from the Red Sea terminal at Yanbu picked up again, offering an alternative route around the Iran-blocked Strait of Hormuz.

Key Highlights
- Hercules Metals remains focused on advancing its flagship Hercules Project in western Idaho, where the company is developing a potentially significant porphyry copper district.
- The latest exploration update extended mineralization at Southern Flats and strengthened the geological case for potential continuity with the larger Leviathan system.
- Despite encouraging exploration developments, the stock's latest decline highlights valuation sensitivity, speculative trading conditions and the considerable execution risks associated with pre-production Mining companies.
Hercules Metals Corp. is a mineral exploration company focused on advancing its wholly owned Hercules Project in Idaho. The Investment case revolves primarily around the Leviathan porphyry copper system, the Southern Flats discovery and additional district-scale exploration targets. The company's strategy is geared toward creating value through exploration rather than current commercial mine production. Consequently, investor sentiment remains highly sensitive to drilling results, geological interpretation, financing conditions, copper-market expectations and the eventual economic viability of its discoveries.
Why Did Hercules Metals Corp. (TSXV:BIG) Fall by -5.43% on 30 September, 2026?
Hercules Metals shares declined -5.43% on September 30, extending a period of uneven trading and highlighting continued Volatility in TSXV:BIG.
Interestingly, the decline occurred despite the company releasing encouraging exploration results from its Hercules Project on the same day.
Hercules reported that step-out drilling had extended copper porphyry mineralization at the Southern Flats zone. Geological modelling suggests Southern Flats could potentially represent a southern extension of the Leviathan system, although additional drilling is required to establish continuity.
The negative market reaction therefore should not automatically be interpreted as evidence that the drilling update was fundamentally weak. The session may instead reflect profit-taking, elevated expectations, valuation sensitivity or investors requiring additional drilling evidence before assigning greater value to the expanded geological interpretation.
Recent trading has also been volatile, reinforcing the speculative nature of the shares. For an exploration-stage company, positive geological developments do not necessarily translate into immediate share-price appreciation.
The Business model of Hercules Metals Corp.
Hercules Metals operates an exploration-led mining business model.
The company controls a substantial mineral-rights position in western Idaho and is attempting to define a district-scale copper system through geological mapping, Geophysical surveys and drilling.
The Hercules Project hosts the Leviathan porphyry copper discovery alongside Southern Flats and additional targets such as Hook and Pegasus.
Unlike an established copper producer, Hercules does not currently depend on commercial metal sales as its core business. Shareholder value instead depends on exploration success, expansion of mineralized systems and the eventual demonstration that these discoveries could support economically viable development.
This creates significant upside optionality but also substantial uncertainty because exploration success must ultimately progress toward resource definition, technical studies, permitting, financing and potentially mine construction.
Key Reasons Behind Decline
Profit-Taking and Valuation Sensitivity: Hercules has generated substantial investor attention following its copper discoveries. Strong expectations can leave exploration stocks vulnerable when investors decide to lock in gains or reassess how much future exploration success is already reflected in the valuation.
Positive Results but Higher Expectations: The Southern Flats update expanded mineralization and supported the potential connection with Leviathan. However, markets may require further drilling before assigning significant value to geological continuity that has not yet been fully demonstrated.
Exploration Uncertainty: Encouraging drill intersections do not automatically establish an economically viable deposit. Considerable additional exploration is required before the scale, grade continuity and potential Economics of the broader system become sufficiently defined.
Execution Risk: Hercules currently has active drilling focused on extending Leviathan southward and investigating the gap toward Southern Flats. Future results will be important for validating management's geological interpretation.
Funding Considerations: Mineral exploration requires continuing Capital Expenditure before Operating Cash Flow becomes available. Hercules recently completed a private Placement involving its incoming Leadership team, strengthening financial alignment while highlighting the capital requirements associated with an aggressive exploration strategy.
Copper-Market Sensitivity: The long-term investment case is closely tied to expectations for copper. Electrification, grid expansion, data centers and infrastructure represent supportive structural themes, but recessionary conditions could weaken near-term industrial Demand expectations.
Geopolitical Uncertainty: US-Iran tensions and wider geopolitical instability can create inflationary pressure through energy markets. Higher fuel and input costs can negatively affect mining-sector economics, while weaker global growth expectations could weigh on copper sentiment.
Risks Investor Needs to Consider
Exploration risk remains the central issue. Hercules has identified substantial mineralization, but considerable work remains before potential economic viability can be established.
Project concentration is another important Factor because much of the company's valuation is linked to the Hercules district.
Permitting, environmental requirements and community engagement could influence future development timelines. As exploration advances toward more intensive activities, regulatory complexity could increase.
Funding and shareholder dilution also Warrant attention. Exploration and eventual project development can require significant amounts of capital.
Commodity volatility represents another risk. A sustained deterioration in copper-market expectations could negatively affect investor appetite for early-stage copper projects regardless of geological progress.
What Is the Dividend Outlook?
Hercules Metals is an exploration-focused company rather than an income-oriented mining business.
Its capital-allocation priorities are expected to remain centered on drilling, geological studies, permitting, project advancement and maintaining sufficient Liquidity to pursue exploration opportunities.
Consequently, dividend distributions are unlikely to represent the central shareholder-return proposition at the current stage of development.
What Does the ESG Investment Case Look Like?
Copper has a potentially supportive ESG demand profile because it is an important material for electrification, power infrastructure and renewable-energy systems.
Hercules' US-focused project location may also appeal to investors interested in strengthening domestic mineral Supply chains.
However, mineral exploration and potential mine development carry environmental considerations involving land disturbance, water management, biodiversity and eventual reclamation requirements.
Social and governance factors include stakeholder engagement, permitting discipline, responsible exploration and effective oversight as the company transitions under its newer leadership structure.

Bull Case:
The Hercules district could continue expanding through successful drilling at Leviathan and Southern Flats.
Potential continuity between the two zones would strengthen the geological scale proposition, while Hook and Pegasus provide additional exploration optionality.
Copper's strategic importance to electricity networks, AI-related infrastructure, renewable energy and electrification could support longer-term interest in large North American copper discoveries.
Continued drilling success represents the most important potential catalyst.
Bear Case:
Hercules remains an exploration-stage company, meaning geological potential has not yet translated into commercial mining operations.
Future drilling could Fail to demonstrate the continuity or scale currently anticipated by investors.
Capital requirements, permitting challenges, shareholder dilution and commodity-market weakness could also pressure valuation.
After substantial investor interest in the discovery story, elevated expectations create additional downside risk if exploration results fail to exceed increasingly demanding market assumptions.

- Resistance Levels: Previous areas associated with selling pressure could limit initial recovery attempts.
- Volume Trends: Strong Volume accompanying declines may signal increased distribution, while improving participation during rebounds would provide better evidence of renewed demand.
- Momentum Indicators: Near-term momentum has weakened, making sustained stabilization more important than isolated positive sessions.
